claim: An AssumeRole call can request a session from 900 seconds (15 minutes) up to the role's maximum session duration setting, and that setting itself can be from 1 hour to 12 hours.
question: What is the minimum and the maximum DurationSeconds an AssumeRole call can request?

qualifiers.condition: bounded by the role's maximum session duration setting

evidence.quote: The duration, in seconds, of the role session. The value specified can range from 900 seconds (15 minutes) up to the maximum session duration set for the role. The maximum session duration setting can have a value from 1 hour to 12 hours. If you specify a value higher than this setting or the administrator setting (whichever is lower), the operation fails.
Valid Range: Minimum value of 900. Maximum value of 43200.

note: d001. A DurationSeconds above the role setting makes the call fail; it is not silently capped.

claim: When an AssumeRole call omits DurationSeconds, the role session lasts 3600 seconds (one hour).
question: How long does an AssumeRole session last when DurationSeconds is not specified?

evidence.quote: By default, the value is set to `3600` seconds.
If users don't specify a value for the `DurationSeconds` parameter, their security credentials are valid for one hour.

claim: A role's maximum session duration setting can be from 1 hour to 12 hours; when no value is set the default maximum of 1 hour applies, and the setting does not limit sessions assumed by AWS services.
question: What range can a role's maximum session duration setting take, and what is its default?

qualifiers.condition: does not limit sessions assumed by AWS services

evidence.quote: This setting can have a value from 1 hour to 12 hours. If you do not specify a value, the default maximum of 1 hour is applied. This setting does not limit sessions assumed by AWS services.

note: d002. Changing the setting takes effect at the next assume; existing sessions keep running.

claim: Role chaining (using one role's credentials to assume a second role) limits the session to a maximum of one hour regardless of the roles' maximum session duration settings; a DurationSeconds above one hour makes the operation fail.
question: What is the longest session when a role is assumed through role chaining, and what happens if a longer DurationSeconds is requested?

qualifiers.scope: per role session obtained through role chaining
qualifiers.condition: applies regardless of the maximum session duration configured for individual roles

evidence.quote: Role chaining limits your AWS Management Console, AWS CLI or AWS API role session to a maximum of one hour. It applies regardless of the maximum session duration configured for individual roles.
However, if you assume a role using role chaining and provide a `DurationSeconds` parameter value greater than one hour, the operation fails.

claim: Role chaining is using a role to assume a second role; it can be done by switching roles in the console, with the CLI or with the API, and transitive session tags are passed to every later session in the chain.
question: What is role chaining?

values.display: use a role to assume a second role
values.spoken: use a role to assume a second role

values.display: transitive session tags are passed to all subsequent sessions in a role chain
values.spoken: transitive session tags pass down the chain

evidence.quote: Role chaining is when you use a role to assume a second role. You can perform role chaining through the AWS Management Console by switching roles, the AWS CLI, or API.
When you assume a role, you can pass a session tag and set the tag as transitive. Transitive session tags are passed to all subsequent sessions in a role chain.

claim: AssumeRoleWithSAML credentials last one hour by default; DurationSeconds can request from 900 seconds (15 minutes) up to the role's maximum session duration, and the session ends at the SAML response's SessionNotOnOrAfter time if that is sooner.
question: What is the default and the allowed session length for AssumeRoleWithSAML?

qualifiers.condition: whichever is shorter: DurationSeconds or the SAML SessionNotOnOrAfter value

evidence.quote: By default, the temporary security credentials created by `AssumeRoleWithSAML` last for one hour. However, you can use the optional `DurationSeconds` parameter to specify the duration of your session. Your role session lasts for the duration that you specify, or until the time specified in the SAML authentication response's `SessionNotOnOrAfter` value, whichever is shorter. You can provide a `DurationSeconds` value from 900 seconds (15 minutes) up to the maximum session duration setting for the role.

claim: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity credentials last one hour by default; DurationSeconds can request from 900 seconds (15 minutes) up to the role's maximum session duration setting, which can be from 1 hour to 12 hours.
question: What is the default and the allowed session length for AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity?

qualifiers.condition: bounded by the role's maximum session duration setting

evidence.quote: By default, the temporary security credentials created by `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` last for one hour. However, you can use the optional `DurationSeconds` parameter to specify the duration of your session. You can provide a value from 900 seconds (15 minutes) up to the maximum session duration setting for the role. This setting can have a value from 1 hour to 12 hours.

claim: GetSessionToken for an IAM user accepts durations from 900 seconds (15 minutes) to 129,600 seconds (36 hours), with 43,200 seconds (12 hours) as the default.
question: What DurationSeconds range and default does GetSessionToken allow for an IAM user?

qualifiers.scope: per GetSessionToken call by an IAM user

evidence.quote: The duration, in seconds, that the credentials should remain valid. Acceptable durations for IAM user sessions range from 900 seconds (15 minutes) to 129,600 seconds (36 hours), with 43,200 seconds (12 hours) as the default.

By default, temporary security credentials for an IAM user are valid for a maximum of 12 hours. But you can request a duration as short as 15 minutes or as long as 36 hours using the `DurationSeconds` parameter.

claim: When GetSessionToken is called with root user credentials, the session is limited to a maximum of 3,600 seconds (one hour); a longer requested duration defaults to one hour.
question: How long can a GetSessionToken session last when the root user calls it?

qualifiers.scope: per GetSessionToken call by the root user

evidence.quote: Sessions for AWS account owners are restricted to a maximum of 3,600 seconds (one hour). If the duration is longer than one hour, the session for AWS account owners defaults to one hour.
For security reasons, a token for an AWS account root user is restricted to a duration of one hour.

claim: GetFederationToken sessions can last from 900 seconds (15 minutes) to 129,600 seconds (36 hours), with 43,200 seconds (12 hours) as the default; with root user credentials the session is limited to 3,600 seconds (one hour).
question: What DurationSeconds range and default does GetFederationToken allow, and what is the maximum with root credentials?

values.spoken: one hour for the root user

qualifiers.condition: root user credentials are limited to one hour

evidence.quote: The duration, in seconds, that the session should last. Acceptable durations for federation sessions range from 900 seconds (15 minutes) to 129,600 seconds (36 hours), with 43,200 seconds (12 hours) as the default. Sessions obtained using root user credentials are restricted to a maximum of 3,600 seconds (one hour).

claim: A console switch-role session lasts 1 hour by default and an IAM user console session 12 hours by default; the switched session gets the role's maximum session duration or the time left in the user session, whichever is less, and assuming a role cannot extend the session.
question: How long does a console switch-role session last and what bounds it?

qualifiers.condition: role maximum session duration or the remaining time in the user session, whichever is less

evidence.quote: When you switch roles, your AWS Management Console session lasts for 1 hour by default. IAM user sessions are 12 hours by default, other users might have different session durations defined. When you switch roles in the console, you are granted the role maximum session duration, or the remaining time in your user session, whichever is less. You can't extend your session duration by assuming a role.

In the AWS Management Console, IAM user sessions are 12 hours by default. IAM users who switch roles in the console are granted the role maximum session duration, or the remaining time in the user's session, whichever is less.

claim: An assume-role call can pass one inline JSON session policy and up to 10 managed policy ARNs, and the plaintext of inline and managed session policies together cannot exceed 2,048 characters.
question: How many managed policy ARNs and how many characters can session policies passed to AssumeRole hold?

values.spoken: up to ten managed policy ARNs

qualifiers.condition: inline and managed session policies combined

evidence.quote: You can pass a single JSON policy document to use as an inline session policy. You can also specify up to 10 managed policy Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) to use as managed session policies. The plaintext that you use for both inline and managed session policies can't exceed 2,048 characters.
You can pass a single JSON inline session policy document using the `Policy` parameter. You can use the `PolicyArns` parameter to specify up to 10 managed session policies.

claim: A session's permissions are the intersection of the identity-based policies of the user or role that created the session and the session policies; a session policy can never grant more than the identity-based policy allows, and an explicit deny in any policy wins.
question: How do session policies combine with the role's own permissions?

values.display: the intersection of the identity-based policies
values.spoken: the intersection with the identity-based policy

values.display: An explicit deny in any of these policies overrides the allow
values.spoken: an explicit deny anywhere overrides the allow

evidence.quote: The permissions for a session are the intersection of the identity-based policies for the IAM entity (user or role) used to create the session and the session policies. Permissions can also come from a resource-based policy. An explicit deny in any of these policies overrides the allow.
You cannot use session policies to grant more permissions than those allowed by the identity-based policy of the role that is being assumed.

claim: STS requests made with AWS credentials share a default quota of 600 requests per second per account per Region; for a cross-account AssumeRole only the calling account's quota is consumed.
question: What is the default STS request quota per account per Region, and which account's quota does a cross-account AssumeRole consume?

values.spoken: six hundred STS requests per second

qualifiers.condition: requests made using AWS credentials; service principals do not consume it

evidence.quote: For example, if an AWS account makes 100 GetCallerIdentity requests per second and 100 AssumeRole calls per second in the same region, that account is consuming 200 of its available 600 STS requests per second for that region.
For cross-account AssumeRole requests, only the account making the AssumeRole request impacts the STS quota. The target account does not have any of it’s quota consumed.
To request an increase to STS request quotas, please open a ticket with AWS support.
